@graph.description: Tilt is the emotional state where your trading plan stops governing. Meet the tilt family tree (giveback, revenge trading, overtrading, FOMO), the two-layer body-plus-behavior early-warning scan, and the detection protocol that stops damage before it compounds.
@graph.headline: Tilt in Trading: The In-Session State That Produces Every Costly Mistake (Family Frame + Detection Protocol)

acceptedAnswer.text: Tilt is emotional decision-making after a loss or a string of losses: increasing your size to recover, abandoning your entry rules, adding to losers. The defining mark is not the emotion itself — it is that the plan has stopped governing. The market is still the market, but you are no longer you.

The widely cited origin is the pinball machine: a frustrated player physically tilts the machine to save the ball, the machine flashes TILT, freezes the flippers, and the ball is lost for certain. Poker adopted the word for the frustrated, over-aggressive play that follows a bad beat; trading inherited it. The metaphor holds across all three: frustration-driven over-aggression is self-punishing.

mainEntity.name: Where does the term "on tilt" come from?

acceptedAnswer.text: Run the two-layer scan. The body: shallow rapid breathing, sweaty palms, tightened jaw or neck, racing heartbeat, feeling flushed. The tilt-specific behavior tells: bigger risk suddenly feeling rational, the get-it-back-right-now thought looping, watching the rupee P&L instead of the chart, autopilot clicks and fat-finger errors, the planned window quietly reopening. Any two signals from either layer means stop for at least 30 minutes.

mainEntity.name: How do I know if I'm on tilt?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. C-game is the trader; tilt is the in-session state that produces C-game behavior; revenge trading is one of the behaviors tilt wears. Tilt is the state where the plan stops governing; revenge trading is the specific post-loss form — the recovery trade driven by the feeling that the loss is a debt the market owes you. Same circuit breaker, same cure.

mainEntity.name: Is revenge trading the same as tilt?

acceptedAnswer.text: Catch the state first with the two-layer scan: any two signals from either layer equals a circuit breaker, with a minimum 30-minute pause away from the desk. Tilt's share is detection — the post-loss response protocol and the A-plus re-entry filter live in the sibling chapters on revenge trading and overtrading.

mainEntity.name: How do I stop tilting after a loss?

acceptedAnswer.text: Two overlooked trigger classes. First, your physical state: bad sleep, poor food, alcohol, stress outside trading — all of it changes your tilt sensitivity before the first candle. Second, market structure: a stop-out on a volatility spike can trigger a helplessness-and-adrenaline reaction that tilts a calm trader. Run a pre-session audit: rate your emotional intensity 1 to 10 — if you are already at 6 before the first trade, you are starting tilted, and the day starts with reduced size or not at all.
